+def get_uptime_facts(module):

diff --git a/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py b/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py

index 0000000..4a7178d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+import errno
+
+import pytest
+
+from units.compat.mock import Mock
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts import sysctl
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware import darwin, freebsd, netbsd, openbsd
+
+
+def make_module(result=(0, '', '')):
+    module = Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = result
+    return module
+
+
+def test_get_sysctl_formats_multiline_and_malformed_lines():
+    output = ('hw.ncpu=4\n'
+              'kern.osrelease: 7.5\n'
+              'kernel.hostname = server\n'
+              'machdep.dmi.system-vendor Vendor Name\n'
+              'kern.message: first line\n'
+              '    second line\n'
+              'malformed\n'
+              'hw.model: CPU\n')
+    module = make_module((0, output, ''))
+
+    assert sysctl.get_sysctl(module, ['hw', 'kern']) == {
+        'hw.ncpu': '4',
+        'kern.osrelease': '7.5',
+        'kernel.hostname': 'server',
+        'machdep.dmi.system-vendor': 'Vendor Name',
+        'kern.message': 'first line\n    second line',
+        'hw.model': 'CPU',
+    }
+    module.run_command.assert_called_once_with(['/sbin/sysctl', 'hw', 'kern'])
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with(
+        'Unable to split sysctl line (malformed): not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure, warning', [
+    ((1, 'hw.ncpu=4', 'permission denied'), 'Unable to read sysctl: permission denied'),
+    (OSError(errno.EIO, 'read failed'), 'Unable to read sysctl: [Errno 5] read failed'),
+])
+def test_get_sysctl_command_failure(failure, warning):
+    module = make_module()
+    if isinstance(failure, tuple):
+        module.run_command.return_value = failure
+    else:
+        module.run_command.side_effect = failure
+
+    assert sysctl.get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with(warning)
+
+
+def test_get_sysctl_missing_binary():
+    module = make_module()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = None
+
+    assert sysctl.get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once_with('Unable to read sysctl: sysctl binary not found')
+    module.run_command.assert_not_called()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('hardware_class', [
+    freebsd.FreeBSDHardware,
+    netbsd.NetBSDHardware,
+    openbsd.OpenBSDHardware,
+    darwin.DarwinHardware,
+])
+def test_bsd_uptime(hardware_class, mocker):
+    module = make_module((0, '1000\n', ''))
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=1234.9)
+
+    assert hardware_class(module).get_uptime_facts() == {'uptime_seconds': 234}
+    module.run_command.assert_called_once_with(['/sbin/sysctl', '-n', 'kern.boottime'])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('result', [(1, '', 'error'), (0, '', ''), (0, 'not numeric', ''),
+                                    (0, '{ sec = 1000, usec = 0 }', '')])
+def test_bsd_uptime_omits_invalid_boot_time(result):
+    module = make_module(result)
+    assert sysctl.get_uptime_facts(module) == {}
+
+
+def test_bsd_uptime_missing_binary():
+    module = make_module()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        sysctl.get_uptime_facts(module)
+    module.run_command.assert_not_called()
+
+
+def test_bsd_uptime_binary_disappears():
+    module = make_module()
+    module.run_command.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'No such file or directory')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        sysctl.get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('hardware_class, other_methods', [
+    (freebsd.FreeBSDHardware, ['get_memory_facts', 'get_dmi_facts',
+                               'get_device_facts', 'get_mount_facts']),
+    (netbsd.NetBSDHardware, ['get_memory_facts', 'get_dmi_facts', 'get_mount_facts']),
+    (darwin.DarwinHardware, ['get_memory_facts', 'get_mac_facts']),
+])
+def test_bsd_populate_includes_uptime_and_cpu(hardware_class, other_methods, mocker):
+    module = make_module((0, '1000', ''))
+    hardware = hardware_class(module)
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=1234)
+    if hardware_class is netbsd.NetBSDHardware:
+        mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.netbsd.get_sysctl', return_value={})
+    if hardware_class is darwin.DarwinHardware:
+        mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.darwin.get_sysctl', return_value={})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_cpu_facts', return_value={'processor_count': 2})
+    for name in other_methods:
+        mocker.patch.object(hardware, name, return_value={})
+
+    assert hardware.populate() == {'processor_count': 2, 'uptime_seconds': 234}
+
+
+def test_openbsd_populate_keeps_all_fact_sources(mocker):
+    module = make_module()
+    hardware = openbsd.OpenBSDHardware(module)
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.openbsd.get_sysctl', return_value={})
+    sources = {
+        'get_processor_facts': {'processor_count': 2},
+        'get_memory_facts': {'memtotal_mb': 1024},
+        'get_device_facts': {'devices': ['sd0']},
+        'get_dmi_facts': {'system_vendor': 'vendor'},
+        'get_mount_facts': {'mounts': []},
+        'get_uptime_facts': {'uptime_seconds': 234},
+    }
+    for name, facts in sources.items():
+        mocker.patch.object(hardware, name, return_value=facts)
+
+    assert hardware.populate() == dict((key, value) for facts in sources.values()
+                                       for key, value in facts.items())
+    for name in sources:
+        getattr(hardware, name).assert_called_once_with()
